title: Yellow at twenty hours
objective: Start phototherapy by plotting the hour-specific bilirubin against thresholds set by gestational age and the infant's neurotoxicity risks, and recognize acute bilirubin encephalopathy before it becomes kernicterus
secondaryObjectives: Tell physiologic from pathologic jaundice, treating jaundice in the first 24 hours as pathologic, and know the risk factors for severe hyperbilirubinemia
Recognize and manage hyperbilirubinemia, hydrops fetalis and the infant of a diabetic mother

brief.situation: 14:00 in the NICU. You are the nurse for Baby Lin, a girl born at 36 weeks, now 20 hours old, admitted at 6 hours for poor feeding. Her mother is type O positive; the baby's blood type and direct antiglobulin test (DAT) came back this morning.
handover: The night nurse thought she 'looked a bit yellow' at 08:00. A total serum bilirubin was drawn at 13:30 and has just resulted.
She is sleepier than at the last feed and took only 10 mL by bottle.

Unit standing order: start phototherapy when the hour-specific bilirubin is at or above the threshold for the infant's gestational age and risk factors, and call the nurse practitioner; the threshold charts are on the unit's computer.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

source.note: Bilirubin keeps rising toward neurotoxic levels without phototherapy. FLAG. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.

why.question: What does Baby Lin's bilirubin mean, and what do you do?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: Jaundice in the first 24 hours is pathologic; with isoimmune hemolysis and 36 weeks' gestation her threshold is lower; plotted by hour she is above phototherapy and near escalation; sleepiness and a weak suck can be early encephalopathy.
parts.modelAnswer: Yellow at 20 hours isn't normal. She's hemolyzing and she's 36 weeks, so her line is lower, and plotted by hour she's over it and close to escalation. Sleepy with a weak suck could be early encephalopathy.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Starts phototherapy now, calls the provider at once for repeat level and exchange readiness, checks neuro status repeatedly, does not defer lights or give water.
parts.modelAnswer: Lights on now, call the nurse practitioner, get the repeat level and exchange prep going, and keep checking her tone and suck. Don't hold the lights or give water.

noProgress.rationale: A bilirubin above the phototherapy threshold untreated an hour on is harm here.

abe.headline: Acute bilirubin encephalopathy
abe.body: Jaundice in the first 24 hours is pathologic. Plot the hour-specific value against her gestational age and risks and start phototherapy without delay.

safe.headline: Plotted, treated, escalated
safe.body: You read early jaundice as pathologic, plotted by hour, gestation and risk, started phototherapy and called within minutes. That is the expert path.

safeGaps.headline: Escalated, with gaps
safeGaps.body: Check whether you plotted by hour and risk, how long phototherapy waited, and how soon you called.

time_up.body: A value above threshold means phototherapy now.

scoring.modelReasoning: Jaundice in the first 24 hours of life is pathologic, often from hemolysis, as here (DAT positive). Bilirubin is read by the infant's age in hours against thresholds set by gestational age and neurotoxicity risk factors; at 36 weeks with hemolysis, 13.2 at 19.5 hours is above her phototherapy threshold and within 2 mg/dL of escalation. Start intensive phototherapy now and call the provider at once; a value near the escalation line needs a repeat level and preparation for exchange. Sleepiness and a poor suck are early signs of acute bilirubin encephalopathy; stupor, arching and a high-pitched cry are later ones.

abeQ.ask: While the plan is set: which are early signs of acute bilirubin encephalopathy?

choices.label: Sleepiness, poor suck and feeding, hypotonia

abeQ.explain: Early: sleepiness or decreased alertness, poor sucking and feeding, hypotonia; later: stupor, hypertonia, arching and a high-pitched cry.
